candidates.statement: This guidance provides information on the implementation of section 505(o)(4) of the Federal 17 Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 355(o)(4)). Section 505(o)(4) authorizes 18 FDA to require application holders for certain drugs 2 to make labeling changes based on new 19 safety information (NSI) (including information related to reduced effectiveness) that becomes 20 available after approval of the drug that FDA determines should be included in the labeling of 21 the drug. This draft guidance revises the guidance for industry Safety Labeling Changes— 22 Implementation of Section 505(o)(4) of the FD&C Act issued in July 2013. After it has been 23 finalized, this guidance will replace the July 2013 guidance. Significant changes from the 2013 24 version include the addition of information related to Congress’ 2018 changes to the statutory 25 definition of adverse drug experience 3 regarding reduced effectiveness, and a description of how 26 FDA reviews and acts on safety labeling changes (SLCs) when NSI applies to multiple 27 application holders and the SLC is issued to multiple applicants. Furthermore, the guidance 28 clarifies when FDA may disclose SLC notification and order letters. Finally, additional changes 29 were made to reflect current SLC processes and procedures that have been updated since the 30 SLC guidance was issued in 2013. 31

candidates.statement: The SLC provisions in section 505(o)(4) apply to the above-listed drugs, including drugs that are 45 not marketed, unless FDA has withdrawn approval of the NDA or ANDA and notice of the 46 withdrawal has been published in the Federal Register , or, in the case of a BLA, the U.S. 47 biologics license to manufacture the biological product has been revoked. Thus, even if an 48 application holder is not actively marketing the drug(s) approved under its NDA, ANDA, or 49 BLA, it is required to make the applicable SLCs under section 505(o)(4) unless and until 50 approval of the application is effectively withdrawn in a Federal Register notice or the U.S. 51 biologics license to manufacture the product has been revoked. 52

candidates.statement: It is FDA’s view that the statutory definition of new safety information is broad to enable FDA to 97 require application holders to add information about serious risks to the labeling of a drug when 98 the Agency determines that such information should be included. 99
candidates.context: The phrases serious risk and unexpected serious risk are also defined in section 505-1(b) of the 94 FD&C Act and are included in the Glossary at the end of this guidance. 95 In 2018, the Substance Use-Disorder Prevention that Promotes Opioid Recovery and Treatment 101 for Patients and Communities Act (SUPPORT Act) (Public Law 115-271) was enacted. Among 102 other things, the SUPPORT Act changed the statutory definition of adverse drug experience in 103 section 505-1(b)(1). It specified that the category of “any failure of expected pharmacological 104 action of the drug” “ may include reduced effectiveness under the conditions of use prescribed in 105 the labeling of such drug, but which may not include reduced effectiveness that is in accordance 106 with such labeling” (section 505-1(b)(1)(E) of the FD&C Act) (emphasis added). candidates.context: The SUPPORT Act added the following italicized language in the revisions to section 505(o)(4) 113 regarding the standard for SLCs: 114 This additional statutory language related to reduced effectiveness clarifies that the Agency can 122 require changes to labeling to include information about a serious risk that results from reduced 123 effectiveness, including information that was derived from a postapproval study or clinical trial 124 required under section 505(o)(3) of the FD&C Act. 7 FDA generally intends to require labeling 125 changes only when the “new information” that the Agency becomes aware of is about a serious 126 risk as defined in section 505-1. 127

candidates.statement: To propose alternative labeling changes that reflect the new safety information in response to the 221 SLC notification letter, the application holder should submit a PAS. Whether the application 222 holder submits a CBE-0 supplement or a PAS, to facilitate the review of the supplement, FDA 223 recommends that the application holder provide a clean version (in Microsoft Word file format) 224 of the labeling (i.e., no redline/strikeout and no annotations) containing the proposed changes 225 and a marked-up version (in Microsoft Word file format) of the labeling. candidates.statement: If the application holder submits a rebuttal statement and FDA does not accept the reasons why 274 labeling changes are not warranted, FDA will initiate a discussion period with the application 275 holder. 18 The discussion period would begin on the date that FDA receives the application 276 holder’s rebuttal statement and last no more than 30 days (unless an extension is warranted). 19 If 277 the application holder agrees to submit a labeling supplement during the discussion period, the 278 supplement should be submitted before the end of the discussion period (and any extension 279 period, if applicable), and FDA will follow the procedure as outlined in the previous section. 280

candidates.statement: Based on the discussion period, the Agency may revise the proposed labeling changes from what 312 was included in the original SLC notification letter. The Agency intends to inform all 313 application holders of any change in the proposed labeling, and application holders should 314 submit that revised proposed labeling for approval before the end of the discussion period. The 315 proposed labeling should be in the form of an amendment to their previously submitted 316 supplement or, if they previously submitted a rebuttal statement, a labeling supplement. If any 317 application holder fails to submit the final proposed labeling before the end of the discussion 318 period, the Agency can order that application holder to make the changes under section 319 505(o)(4)(E) of the FD&C Act and as described in section III.D of this guidance. An order 320 issued to one or more application holders will not delay approval of labeling changes for the rest 321 of the application holders. 322

candidates.context: Under section 505(o)(4)(F) of the FD&C Act, if the application holder neither submits a labeling 429 supplement within 15 days of the date of the SLC order nor initiates dispute resolution within 5 430 days of the date of the SLC order, the application holder will be in violation of the statute. This 431 may result in enforcement actions, which are described in section V of this guidance. 432 FDA expects that new approved labeling with SLCs will be available on the application holder’s 436 website within 10 days of the date listed on the approval of the labeling supplement. In addition, 437 approved updates to NDA and BLA labeling with SLCs are posted on FDA’s website. 27

candidates.context: An application holder may appeal an SLC order using formal dispute resolution procedures. 29 Under section 505(o)(4)(F) of the FD&C Act, the application holder must make its appeal of the 454 SLC order within 5 days of receiving that order. FDA has interpreted 5 days to mean 5 calendar 455 days . Appeals received by FDA later than 5 days after the date the SLC order letter was received 456 will not be considered. Similarly, for appeals to higher levels, such as the Center director, 457 application holders should appeal a written determination made by a previous level within 5 days 458 of receiving that determination. FDA will consider the dispute resolution process to be 459 concluded if an appeal of a written determination is not received within this time frame. 460

candidates.statement: If the application holder neither submits a labeling supplement within 15 days of the date of an 470 SLC order nor initiates dispute resolution within 5 days, the application holder will be in 471 violation of section 505(o)(4) of the FD&C Act. In addition, if at the conclusion of the dispute 472 resolution process, FDA determines that a labeling supplement must be submitted and such 473 supplement is not submitted within 15 days of the date of the determination, the application 474 holder will be in violation of section 505(o)(4) of the FD&C Act. 475
